newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise dented by building, property.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise dented by building, property.

text.p: A strong contribution by Lyonnaise des Eaux' water business helped offset weakness in its building and property activities, but not enough to keep the bourse happy with the first-half results and outlook reported on Thursday.
Lyonnaise chairman Jerome Monod told an analysts meeting the full-year should reflect the first-half result.
The utilities company posted interim net attributable profit up 25 percent to 635 million francs ($123.3 million) but some analysts had been expecting around 700 million francs.
Lyonnaise shares ended down 1.67 percent at 459.20 francs.
First-half sales fell eight percent to 44.37 billion francs.

The services sector contributed a net profit of 715 million francs, of which 596 million came from water, which was up 37 percent. The water division benefited from the acquisition last year of Northumbrian Water Plc.
Lyonnaise owns 63 percent of Northumbrian.
Construction turned in a loss of six million francs, while other construction-related activities made a 56 million profit.
But these were not enough to make up the 26 million in losses from building and public works, and 36 million loss in road building.
Its property sector saw a 104 million franc loss.
Its stock of holdings fell to 2.25 billion francs at mid-year against 2.85 billion a year ago and are expected to fall further to around 1.7-1.8 billion by the end of this year.
"The general objective is to have less than one billion francs of stock in two years' time," Monod said. "The effects of the property crisis are already largely behind us."
He confirmed that GTM Entrepose had opted "to focus on a number of recurrent businesses and that some foreign subsidiaries could be sold." Lyonnaise owns 48 percent of GTM.
Waste treatment contributed a 90 million francs profit, versus 84 million a year ago, while energy profits rose to 60 million from 39 million.

Communications' profit contribution was 37 million francs compared to 48 million. Sales rose 12.6 percent from a year ago, helped by good results of the M6 television channel, in which it is a significant shareholder, and cable activities, which saw turnover up 7.5 percent from a year ago.
Lyonnaise also owns 10 percent of the Television Par Satellite (TPS) digitial television joint venture set up with TF1, France Television, M6 and Luxembourg's CLT.
Monod said he expected TPS to break even by 2000, after total investment of 2.5 billion francs, with 700,000 customers.

The group wants to maintain its "world leadership" in the water business by building up a portfolio of "young" major contracts, he said. Just over half the group's sales came from water, and again more than half of the water business came from outside France.
Finance director Antoine Giscard d'Estaing said 83 percent of capital expenditure was in the water sector where cashflow was strongest.
-- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.152 French Francs)
